Variants.Content: Witnessing the devastating wounds inflicted by Iberian iron blades, Scipio Africanus standardized the 'Gladius Hispaniensis' (Spanish Sword) across his legions after capturing the armories of Carthago Nova. Employing superior high-carbon steel, its double-edged blade was ideal for both ferocious slashing and fatal pelvic thrusts behind the scutum, revolutionizing Roman infantry doctrine.
